valuation_philosophy: Chorus is a regulated, high-leverage, income-oriented fibre network utility, not a growth compounder. The correct framing is dividend-plus-modest-growth (FY2025 dividend 57.5cps ~6.0% yield at $9.55; FY2026 guided 60cps ~6.3% yield), underpinned by the Commerce Commission's PQ2 (2025-2028) building-blocks/RAB revenue-and-capex framework and a post-UFB-build capex taper that is inflecting reported FCF from structurally negative (-$258m FY2018) to positive and rising ($162m FY2025). This DCF is built on UNLEVERED (enterprise) owner FCF -- EBIT*(1-cash tax)+D&A-capex, with NO interest deduction -- discounted at WACC, with the ~NZ$3.18bn net debt subtracted once from enterprise value to reach equity value. This is standard enterprise-DCF practice and is essential here because Chorus's REPORTED FCF (OCF-capex, used in the Metrics.csv) is LEVERED (net of ~$175-220m/yr cash interest paid), and discounting levered FCF at WACC while also subtracting net debt would double-count Chorus's leverage. The reported/levered FCF series and its margin are disclosed separately below for audit; the DCF engine runs on the unlevered series. Given a market cap of only ~$4.25bn against ~$3.18bn of net debt (net debt is ~75% of the current market cap and ~4.5x EBITDA), the equity value is extremely sensitive to WACC -- see the sensitivity matrix, which shows intrinsic value ranging from ~$10.68 at 5% WACC down to ~$5.9-6.1 at 9% WACC on an unchanged FCF path. This is a mechanical consequence of leverage (a fixed-dollar net debt deduction against a discount-rate-sensitive enterprise value), not a modelling artefact.

growth_rate_rejections.equity_cagr_rejected: Shareholders' equity has COLLAPSED from NZ$1,022m (FY2018) to NZ$430m (H1-2026, 31-Dec-2025), a 3yr CAGR of approximately -18%/yr and 5yr CAGR of approximately -9%/yr. This is NOT economic decline -- it is the mechanical result of Chorus paying dividends (70-90% of net operating FCF policy, raised Feb-2024) that exceed near-zero-to-modest reported net income (FY2023 +$25m, FY2024 -$9m, FY2025 +$4m) every year, steadily eroding the equity base through retained-earnings deficits while the underlying regulated asset base and cash generation are actually IMPROVING. Using equity CAGR as a growth driver would imply a business in terminal decline, which contradicts every operating metric (fibre uptake rising toward 80% target, EBITDA rising, capex falling, FCF inflecting positive). Equity CAGR is discarded entirely; revenue/EBITDA growth is used instead.
growth_rate_rejections.pe_and_net_income_rejected: Reported net income has been near zero or negative for the past three years (FY2023 +$25m, FY2024 -$9m, FY2025 +$4m, H1-2026 +$15m) despite EBITDA of ~NZ$700-725m, because ~NZ$400-475m/yr of depreciation & amortisation (post-UFB-build asset base, plus accelerated depreciation on the copper network being retired by 2028) and ~NZ$175-220m/yr of cash interest on ~NZ$3.2-3.3bn of debt consume nearly all of EBIT. A P/E multiple on Chorus is meaningless (FY2025 P/E on 1cps EPS would be ~870x; H1-2026 annualised is similarly distorted) and is not used anywhere in this valuation or in the Step 8c historical multiple sanity check (P/B and EV/EBITDA are used instead, which are meaningful given the large non-cash D&A charge and high leverage).

inputs.net_debt_basis: H1 FY2026 (31 December 2025) balance sheet: total debt $3,336m, cash $161m.
inputs.niffco_monetisation_note: On 7-Aug-2026 the NZ Crown announced binding agreements to monetise (sell down) its NIFFCo debt/securities linked to the original UFB build (book value ~$642m, net proceeds to the Crown ~$702m). This is a transaction on the CROWN's side of the NIFFCo structure, not a repayment or restructuring of CHORUS's own debt or CIP securities -- Chorus has explicitly stated it does not anticipate material changes to the terms and conditions of its own securities as a result. ASSUMPTION MADE: net debt above is left UNADJUSTED for this event -- it is treated as a change in the ultimate holder of existing Crown-linked paper, not a change in the cash flows or balance-sheet obligations of Chorus itself. If subsequent disclosure shows the monetisation triggers any repricing, acceleration, or restructuring of Chorus's own CIP/Crown funding lines, net debt and this valuation should be revisited.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 actual (OCF $559m - gross capex $397m); this is LEVERED free cash flow (net of cash interest paid).
inputs.last_fcf_basis: Year-1 (FY2026E) UNLEVERED owner FCF from the component build: EBIT*(1-cash tax)+D&A-capex, excluding SBC (immaterial) and excluding interest (handled via WACC discounting + net debt subtraction, not as an FCF deduction). This is materially higher than reported FY2025 FCF of $162m because reported FCF is LEVERED (net of ~$175-220m/yr cash interest); see valuation_philosophy.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual Report FY2024 note 'Key management personnel compensation': share-based payments of NZ$1,638k (thousands) disclosed for FY2023 KMP only; NZ$0 for FY2024 ('performance hurdles were not met for the long-term performance share scheme'). Chorus does not disclose a broader company-wide SBC expense line in the P&L or cash flow statement -- SBC is genuinely immaterial (KMP long-term incentive scheme only, <0.2% of revenue even at its highest disclosed level) and does not move this valuation; it is deducted for completeness at a flat 0.15% of revenue.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income (interest income) is trivial (~$1-2m/yr per H1-2026 income statement) and is NOT stripped from FCF because Chorus holds NET DEBT (not net cash) -- the 'strip interest income when net cash > 1x FCF base' rule does not apply to a net-debt company. No double-counting risk exists here in the direction the rule guards against.

historical_growth.eps_note: EPS/net income CAGR not computed -- meaningless given near-zero/negative net income (FY2023-25); see growth_rate_rejections.pe_and_net_income_rejected.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Reported and owner FCF CAGRs are not computable over 3yr/5yr windows because the FY2018/FY2020 base years were structurally negative (UFB build capex peak, -$258m/-$205m); a CAGR from a negative base is undefined. FY2022->FY2025 (52->162) grew ~46%/yr off a tiny base as capex tapered -- illustrative of the inflection, not a repeatable growth rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-9% to -18%/yr) diverges enormously (>30%) from Revenue/EBITDA CAGR (+1-2%/yr). Per growth_rate_rejections.equity_cagr_rejected, this divergence is a DISTRIBUTION-POLICY artefact (dividends >> net income), not an operating signal, and equity CAGR is explicitly discarded as the growth driver in favour of revenue/EBITDA, which are the metrics the Commerce Commission's RAB/PQ regime actually caps and grows.
historical_growth.notes: Growth here is REGULATED (Commerce Commission building-blocks/RAB regime under PQ2, 2025-2028), not market-driven -- base-case projected growth (2.3-2.8%/yr) reflects RAB growth plus CPI-linked allowances, consistent with 7yr historical revenue CAGR of only 0.34%/yr and EBITDA CAGR of 1.10%/yr, modestly stepped up for the copper-retirement margin tailwind and January-2025 fibre price increase.

wacc_rationale.approach: Bottom-up CAPM build, cross-checked against the Commerce Commission's own PQ2 allowed WACC determination.
wacc_rationale.asset_beta_rationale: Regulated network utility with contracted/RAB-set cash flows typically carries a low unlevered/asset beta (0.35-0.45); 0.40 used.
wacc_rationale.cost_of_debt_basis: H1 FY2026 weighted average interest rate per company disclosure (down from 5.7% HY25 on refinancing)
wacc_rationale.capital_weights_basis: Market-value weights: debt $3,175m net debt / equity market cap ~$4,250m at current price.
wacc_rationale.regulatory_cross_check: The Commerce Commission has SET Chorus's allowed WACC at 7.68% PRE-TAX for the PQ2 period (1-Jan-2025 to 31-Dec-2028), up from 4.72% in the prior period (FY2024 Annual Report, CEO letter). Converted to a rough post-tax equivalent at the 28% statutory rate, that is approximately 5.53% post-tax -- broadly consistent with (slightly below) the 6.02% bottom-up build. The regulatory figure uses the regulator's NOTIONAL benchmark gearing for the RAB, not Chorus's actual capital structure or equity-holder risk, and does not price PQ3 (2029 reset) uncertainty or refinancing risk.
wacc_rationale.risk_addon_rationale: Added on top of the bottom-up build (not stacked as a generic NZ small-cap discount -- explicitly NOT applied, since Chorus is a ~NZ$4.25bn liquid, dual-listed NZX/ASX index constituent with none of the illiquidity risk of the micro-caps elsewhere in this research set) to reflect: (a) PQ3 (from 2029) regulatory reset uncertainty on allowed WACC/RAB rollforward, not captured in the PQ2 number; (b) refinancing/interest-rate risk on the EUR/AUD medium-term note stack recurring through 2032; (c) leverage near the top of Chorus's own 4.75x net-debt/EBITDA policy tolerance, which raises the risk borne by the equity residual claim beyond what the regulatory notional-gearing WACC assumes.
wacc_rationale.bull_bear_rationale: Bull reflects a favourable PQ3 signal and improving credit profile (S&P positive outlook) compressing WACC toward the bottom-up/regulatory-cross-check range; bear reflects adverse PQ3 reset risk, higher-for-longer refinancing rates, and leverage stress.

base.assumption_notes: Growth: PQ2 RAB+CPI-linked revenue cap, tapering toward long-run CPI/GDP (2.3%) as the terminal anchor. EBITDA margin: rises from FY2025's 69.5% toward ~72.3% as copper retirement (accelerated to 2028) removes legacy network opex. D&A: tapers from the H1-2026 run-rate (~42% of revenue, still elevated by accelerated copper depreciation) toward a steady-state ~29% once copper is fully retired (2028, Year 3) and the fibre asset base stops growing. Capex: tapers from FY2026 guidance ($375-415m, used $392m) toward a derived sustaining-only level of ~$230-240m/yr (consistent with management's own HY26 disclosure that sustaining capex was running ~$158m/half = ~$316m/yr annualised with discretionary growth capex fading further as the 80% uptake target is approached). Cash tax: ramped from a low starting rate (10%, reflecting CIP-notional-interest and Crown-grant-amortisation permanent differences that have kept CASH tax paid near zero historically) toward the 28% statutory rate by Year 10 as those Crown-funding-related shelters are assumed to erode, consistent with the Aug-2026 NIFFCo monetisation reducing the CIP structure's role over time. Terminal cap multiple of 8.0x EV/EBITDA was set via the Step 8c sanity check (see sanity_check block) -- an unconstrained 9x cap capitalised Year-10 EBITDA at an implied EV/EBITDA of 10.0x on FY2025 EBITDA, above Chorus's actual 10-year trading range (5.5x-9.7x); 8.0x brings the implied multiple to 9.66x, at the top of but within the historical band.

bull.assumption_notes: Fibre uptake exceeds the 80% target faster, ARPU mix-shift and copper cost-out land at the top end, PQ3 (2029) reset is favourable and credit profile improves (S&P positive outlook realised), compressing WACC and supporting a richer (9.0x) exit multiple -- still only modestly above the historical 3yr-average EV/EBITDA of 9.2x, but the bull IV's 12.4x implied EV/EBITDA on FY2025 EBITDA does exceed the 10yr historical ceiling of 9.7x, i.e. the bull case explicitly requires some multiple re-rating, not just cash-flow delivery.

bear.assumption_notes: FWA/Starlink substitution caps uptake below the 80% target, adverse PQ3 (2029) reset pressures allowed WACC/RAB rollforward, copper withdrawal costs and write-offs run higher than planned, and refinancing at higher-for-longer rates lifts WACC while a de-rating (7.0x, below the historical median of 8.6x) reflects a market pricing in the leverage/regulatory risk.

base.fcf_path_used: base case unlevered owner FCF (decelerating growth path, not a constant rate)
base.interpretation: The 15%-IRR entry price of ~$1.68 sits FAR below both intrinsic value ($8.17) and the current price ($9.55). This is the mechanically correct output, not a formula error: Chorus's projected growth (2.3-2.8%/yr) is far below the 15% hurdle, AND net debt (~$3,175m, a FIXED dollar amount) is ~75% of the current $4.25bn market cap. When cash flows and terminal value are discounted at 15% instead of the 7% WACC, enterprise value shrinks sharply while the fixed net-debt deduction does not -- crushing the thin equity residual. A cross-check computing the ENTIRE DCF at WACC=15% (not just the entry-price hurdle discounting) independently produces an intrinsic value near zero, confirming this is a leverage effect, not a bug. PRACTICALLY: Chorus is not a stock that can be bought today to manufacture a 15% IRR from fundamentals alone -- it is priced (and should be evaluated) as a ~6% dividend-yield regulated-utility income holding, where the relevant comparison is the WACC-based intrinsic value and the dividend yield, not a growth-IRR entry price. See valuation_philosophy.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows are near-flat across terminal growth because the 8.0x EV/EBITDA cap (not Gordon growth) binds the terminal value at every WACC/g combination shown -- Gordon growth only would have produced materially higher (unrealistic) values at low WACC/high-g combinations, which the cap correctly suppresses. The real sensitivity communicated by this matrix is to WACC: intrinsic value ranges from ~$10.68/share at 5% WACC down to ~$5.7-6.1/share at 9% WACC -- an ~80% swing in equity value for a 4-point WACC range, roughly double the swing a similarly-profiled unlevered company would show, which is the direct consequence of Chorus's ~4.5x net-debt/EBITDA leverage. This is the single most important sensitivity in this model and should be surfaced prominently on the dashboard.

sanity_check.methodology: 10-year historical trading multiples computed from Yahoo Finance monthly closes aligned to Chorus's 30-June fiscal year-end, against FY-end shareholders' equity, revenue, and EBITDA. P/E is deliberately EXCLUDED (see growth_rate_rejections.pe_and_net_income_rejected) as meaningless given near-zero/negative net income.
sanity_check.issue_found: An initial base case (terminal EV/EBITDA cap of 9.0x, more aggressive EBITDA-margin ramp and D&A/capex taper) produced an intrinsic value of $9.59, implying an EV/EBITDA of 10.53-10.56x on FY2025 EBITDA -- ABOVE the entire 10-year historical trading range (5.53x-9.71x) and above the current already-elevated 10.53x print. This tripped the sanity check.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Reduced the base-case terminal EV/EBITDA cap from 9.0x to 8.0x and modestly tempered the EBITDA-margin ramp (72.3% vs 73.0% terminal margin) and D&A/capex taper pace. This lowered the base-case intrinsic value to $8.17/share, implying an EV/EBITDA of 9.66x on FY2025 EBITDA -- within (at the top of) the 10-year historical range and close to the recent 3-year average of 9.21x. Implied P/B of 8.45x remains above the historical median (3.52x) but is broadly consistent with the CURRENT market P/B of 9.88x, which itself reflects the structural equity-base collapse from the dividend policy (P/B is a poor anchor for Chorus for exactly this reason -- a shrinking equity denominator mechanically inflates P/B even at an unchanged or falling share price, so EV/EBITDA is the more reliable of the two multiples here).
sanity_check.note_on_pb: P/B for Chorus is trending toward being an unreliable anchor over time precisely because shareholders' equity is shrinking mechanically from the dividend policy (see growth_rate_rejections). EV/EBITDA is weighted more heavily in this sanity check as the meaningful cross-check multiple.

dividend_context.payout_policy: 70-90% of net operating free cash flow (after sustaining capex), raised from 60-80% in Feb-2024; policy explicitly targets dividend growth at the rate of inflation.
dividend_context.note: For an income-oriented holding, the dividend yield (~6.0-6.3% at current price) plus modest inflation-linked dividend growth is a more intuitive way to frame the expected return than a pure capital-appreciation IRR -- see entry_price.base.interpretation.

fcf_quality_history.note: SBC and interest-income adjustments are immaterial for Chorus (net-DEBT company, trivial KMP-only SBC) -- reported and owner FCF are essentially identical historically. The material adjustment is the LEVERED vs UNLEVERED FCF distinction used in the DCF projections; see valuation_philosophy.

data_quality_notes: The Metrics.csv 'FreeCashFlow' column is LEVERED FCF (OCF - capex, net of cash interest paid); this DCF's projections and last_fcf use UNLEVERED owner FCF (EBIT*(1-tax)+D&A-capex) as required for a WACC-discounted enterprise DCF that also subtracts net debt. Do not compare last_fcf directly to historical FreeCashFlow figures without this context.

CY25 RAB capex allocations are unaudited pending the Commerce Commission Information Disclosure due May-2026 per the Analysis JSON; precise current RAB value not independently confirmed from primary regulatory sources.
Aug-2026 NIFFCo monetisation treated as a Crown-side transaction not affecting Chorus's own net debt -- see inputs.niffco_monetisation_note.
SBC is genuinely immaterial (KMP-only long-term incentive scheme, <0.2% of revenue) and does not move this valuation; deducted for completeness only.
